evidence: well_viewer/data/image_identity.py:178-224 classify_filename_role strips the role suffix and its extension once and falls back to _strip_known_ext (line 231) instead of Path(...).stem; probe: classify_filename_role('A1_f1_1.5h_w2_labels.tif') -> (Role.MASK, 'A1_f1_1.5h_w2'). image_resolver.classify_filename_kind (image_resolver.py:130-142) is now a thin wrapper over the same function, so the second copy is gone.

well_viewer/data/image_discovery.py:596-607 (_scan_raw_disk_files): the bare else now logs '[image-load-debug] skip %s kind=%s has no accumulator here' and drops the file instead of doing mask.setdefault(...); the comment names the smFISH-into-load_mask_array rint defect explicitly.

well_viewer/data/frame_load.py:273-284 (_pick inside match_image_ref) now refuses on both axes: 'ambiguous_fov' when fov is empty and hits span >1 FOV, 'ambiguous_tp' when tp is empty and hits span >1 timepoint; both tiers (normalized at 291 and numeric at 310) bail on a status starting with 'ambiguous'.

well_viewer/features/image_browser/image_table/facet_view.py:196-222 _disagreeing_columns finds, per column, any row whose values differ from the single header strip; plan_facets (lines 253-276) skips those columns' inner labels and any group span that overlaps them, and logs a warning naming the count. renderer.py replays the same plan, so export inherits the omission.

well_viewer/features/image_browser/image_table/facet_view.py:179-193 _axis_vals now scans the whole row/column for the first cell that carries any value and only falls back to index 0 when every cell is blank; its docstring names the plate-mode blank-cell case the finding reported.

well_viewer/data/image_resolver.py:153-170 normalize_numeric_token now goes through image_identity.raw_token instead of str(value or ''); probe returns '0' for both 0 and '0' and '' for ''. The docstring names the frame_load.match_image_ref 'match anything' consequence.

well_viewer/data/image_discovery.py:696-714 (find_well_images_and_masks) now logs a warning when a well label does not parse ('the loose-file scan cannot filter by well — images belonging to other wells may be included'), but the comment states outright 'It is not *fixed* here': _scan_raw_disk_files:585 still skips _raw_file_well_passes entirely when well_token is falsy, and data_loading.extract_well_token (line 964) still returns None. The cross-well contamination can still occur; only a log line marks it.

controller.py:787-798 returns from the OVERLAY_CHAN branch without ever calling mark_uncorrected, and image_compose.is_raw_fallback (line 1021-1036) keys on _binary_base(cell['chan']) — for an overlay cell that is the '⊕ OVERLAY' sentinel, which is never a recorded key, so _cell_title's tooltip is silent too. The status line at controller.py:1108 still counts the member-channel fallbacks recorded by frame_load.load_frame_array:365.

well_viewer/core/image_view_state.py:62-72 adds reset_for_new_dataset() clearing both lut_by_channel and tint_by_channel, and core/load_controller.py:412 calls app._app_state.image_view.reset_for_new_dataset() on dataset load.

image_compose._load_ratio_array (line 497-514) loads through _load_array with num_chan/den_chan, and frame_load.load_frame_array:365 records raw_fallbacks under (well, that channel, tp, fov). is_raw_fallback keys on the cell's ratio token, so a ratio cell is never badged while its numerator/denominator channel — absent from the grid — carries the count.

image_compose.composite_column_rgb still calls `use_tophat = _row_display_opts(ctx, r)[0]` with no channel argument (image_compose.py:709); _row_display_opts (line 428) returns (False, False, '') when _channel_opts_for gets chan=None, so a corrected channel lazy-loads the raw frame. git log -L on the region shows it untouched since PR #782.

image_compose._parse_lut:411-416 still falls back to _shared_channel_lut(ctx, row_idx), which reads _row_channel -> cells[row_idx][0]['chan'] (line 356-361) — column 0's channel — even when a chan argument was supplied but has no channel_opts entry. Unchanged since PR #782.

controller.py:1059-1061 passes cell['chan'] (the '⊕ OVERLAY' sentinel for an overlay cell) into _install_cell_events; _hover_array (line 476-500) then calls _load_array with that sentinel, which resolves nothing, so _hover_text returns '' and the readout stays empty for every overlay cell.

well_viewer/data/image_resolver.py:130-142 classify_filename_kind is now documented as 'a thin legacy-vocabulary wrapper' delegating to image_identity.classify_filename_role, with _ROLE_TO_KIND (line 120-127) including Role.PHASE -> 'phase'. There is one classifier and one suffix table.

datasets/merge_plates/merge_plates_compute.py:134-222 merge_sample_definitions now reads both blocks through selections_model.from_block (which validates v2 and migrates v1) and writes the result with to_block, carrying selections, well labels, plot groups, current_id and both notes; the docstring names the emptied-v1-block defect.

datasets/ome_import/apply.py:56-68 convert() now calls destination_problem(dest, src, params) and raises OmeImportError before writing anything, and reads resume_state(...).resumable at line 78 — the check sits in convert(), which is the single path both the page and worker.py's queued start go through.

datasets/validate/apply.py:34,97,137 now use util.json_write.write_json_atomic (tmp in the destination dir + os.replace, permissions preserved), the same call validate/record.py:152 uses; a repo-wide AST guard forbids truncating JSON writes outside a live allowlist.

datasets/merge_plates/apply.py:84-88 _remap._rename still returns _remap_well_field(...)[0] and drops the was_rewritten flag; rewrite_member_field (datasets/_common/member_names.py:119-131) returns the name unchanged for a non-conformant member, so it lands in the destination archive under dataset 2's well token. Only name collisions are refused (_refuse_dropped, line 104-125); _merge_measurements:230-234 leaves the CSV row equally unrewritten, so the dest_in_names check at line 238 still passes.

datasets/import_loose/apply.py:217-235 _zip_well_folders still iterates every directory entry of the folder whose name canonicalises to a well and zips/unlinks its TIFs, with no distinction between folders run_zipper just created and pre-existing ones; import_loose_compute.scan_folder (line 183-215) is still non-recursive and loose-TIF-only, and convert_in_place (line 264-312) adds no warning about the extra scope.

datasets/subset/subset_compute.py:215-225 row_matches still reads float(row['timepoint_hours']) and returns False on a blank/unparsable value, while member_matches (line 182-212) parses the filename's timepoint token — so a legacy CSV with a blank column drops every row while the images copy. subset/apply.py:130-137 _verify still blames the filter ('check that the filter actually matches data in the source dataset').

datasets/_common/dataset_paths.py:187-205 in_containers still assigns containers[well] = zip_path in glob order with no collision detection or warning, so A1.zip and A01.zip collapse silently; the sibling out_csvs (line 208-222) documents its identical overwrite while the input side, which every copy tool trusts, still does not.

datasets/_common/containers.py:385-397: the tier-1 whole-file path now calls publish_container(sources[0], dest), which stages to __aw_tmp_<name>.pid<N> and os.replace()s (containers.py:240-281); an interrupted copy leaves no partial <WELL>.zip.

util/zip_write.py:280-291 atomic_zip now runs zipfile.testzip() (CRC read-back of every member) in addition to the member-list check, gated by a `verify` flag defaulting to `durable`, and raises ZipWriteError without publishing when a member fails.

util/zip_write.py:153-168 replace_folder_with_archive still builds archived_resolved from Path(p).resolve() and compares p.resolve() for each walked file; there is no st_ino/samefile handling and no mention of symlinks or hardlinks anywhere in the module. An in-folder symlink to an archived file still resolves equal (so it is not 'kept' and dies with the rmtree), and an archived path that is itself a symlink out of the folder is dropped from archived_resolved and reported as kept.

WellPlateZipper.py:186-195 folder_well still does place(f, os.path.join(well_dir, os.path.basename(f))) for shutil.copy2/shutil.move with no existence check, then prints f'{well}: {len(files)} files' — the source count, not the survivor count. Under --recursive two same-basename files from different subfolders still collapse silently.

datasets/ome_import/controller.py:52-71 _launch now logs, sets the failed outcome and emits self.jobFinished.emit(False, message, '') before returning on a missing source or destination, so the queue bridge is released.

All three sites still assign inside the suppression: datasets/subset/apply.py:121-122, datasets/merge_plates/apply.py:271-272 and datasets/concatenate/apply.py:438-439 each do `with swallow(f"stat {zip_path}"): entry['seg_fp'] = f"{zip_path.stat().st_mtime_ns}"`, so a failed stat leaves the source dataset's fingerprint on the carried-over override, which validate/apply.py:83 then treats as stale.
